What they found was rats turned into junkies in those conditions. One day a researcher realized that this must be a miserable environment for a rat when all they have to do is eat and shoot dope. So he created a place called Rat Park.

Rat Park was set up to provide a rat with everything he would ever want and need. It was a safe place with other rats to interact with, opposite sex rats to get it on with, and opportunities for novel stimulation. What was found was that rats would not become junkies in such conditions. Even rats that were junkies in a cage by themselves were not junkies in Rat Park. Even when they were made addicted in Rat Park, they reverted to non-addiction.

Rat psychology and human psychology are different. Humans are a much more emotionally and socially complex type of creature. Rat Park shows, though, that it's the environment that creates addicts.
